name: Kingdom of Luang Phrabang
native: ອານາຈັກຫຼວງພຣະບາງ

predecessors.name: Lan Xang
predecessors.text: the northern part of Lan Xang, which kept Luang Prabang after the partition of 1707

successors.name: French Indochina
successors.text: the Luang Prabang kingdom east of the Mekong, a protectorate of France from 1893

ledger.x: 1707: Kitsarat is crowned at Luang Prabang and the kingdom is formed.
1707: Muang Phuan becomes a tributary of Luang Prabang.
1792: the first Siamese occupation ends; Anurutha reigns 1792-1819.
A second Siamese occupation ('Siamese occupation (179.. - 2 June 1794)').
2 June 1794: the second Siamese occupation ends ('Siamese occupation (179.. - 2 June 1794)').
7 April 1889: the Sipsong Chau Tai pass to France.
October 1893: Luang Prabang becomes a French protectorate.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1765-1767)
wars.outcome: Vientiane's Ong Boun wrote to Hsinbyushin in October 1764 'urging the Burmese to invade his rival Luang Prabang'; 'Luang Prabang fell to the Burmese in March 1765' and became a Burmese vassal.

wars.name: Lao rebellion (1826-1828)
wars.outcome: 'Anouvong made more direct overtures to Luang Prabang in February 1827,' seeking support and supplies; the page does not say what Luang Prabang did.

wars.name: Haw wars
wars.outcome: 'A particularly destructive attack during the Haw wars by the Chinese Black Flag Army in 1887' reached Luang Prabang; the French conducted campaigns against the Haw in Laos and Tonkin until the 1880s.

wars.name: Franco-Siamese War (1893)
wars.outcome: France forced Siam to cede the lands east of the Mekong; Luang Prabang became a French protectorate and the administrative capital of Laos moved to Vientiane.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line: the borders with Vientiane, Muang Phuan, Burma, Chiang Mai and Tonkin are approximate; the Sipsong Chau Tai and Muang Phuan are tributary margins.

The 1889 French treaty with the White Tai lord of Muang Lay and the 1893 cession of the east bank were fixed by treaty, but the line itself is not given on the pages opened; only the Sipsong Chau Tai frontier is firm.
